$comment: Request/response JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for litellm.postman_collection.json, rendered into its items' descriptions and LITELLM_SCHEMAS.md (linked from LITELLM.md). Edit here, then: uv run --no-sync python scripts/api_schemas.py render litellm. An OPEN subset (additionalProperties: true) of an upstream server, LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0): request schemas checked against the box's GET /openapi.json (621 paths; it declares response bodies only for /key/generate and /user/info), the rest read from LiteLLM's source at the v1.95.0 tag; each entry's `$comment` says which. The OpenAI chat-completions and models entries point to the subset shared with vLLM and llama.cpp (vllm.schemas.json), and the pass-through health items to each service's own entry (same_as). Admin endpoints: shapes only, never values. Checked by unit-tests/apidocs only (tier 1); an image-tag bump re-checks them (ai/litellm/CLAUDE.md).

allowed_passthrough_routes.description: The pass-through prefixes this key may call (`/v1/classifier`, …). Set it INSIDE `metadata`, never as the top-level field of the same name (Enterprise-only, 403 unlicensed); only a proxy admin may set it. LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth

key_fields.$comment: the GenerateKeyRequest / UpdateKeyRequest fields this stack uses (~50 in all)

models.description: The `model_name`s / chain aliases the key may call; empty: all

health_endpoint.description: One deployment's health check, its `litellm_params` minus credentials (`api_base` only for an admin)

GET /health.$comment: litellm/proxy/health_endpoints/_health_endpoints.py at the v1.95.0 tag health_endpoint (the box's GET /openapi.json declares no body); LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).
GET /health.description: Needs a key. Pings every deployment the key may use (or answers the background check's last result).

GET /health/liveliness.$comment: litellm/proxy/health_endpoints/_health_endpoints.py at the v1.95.0 tag health_liveliness; LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).
GET /health/liveliness.description: No key. The container healthcheck's target.

503.description: this copy is shutting down (SIGTERM: a swap deploy retiring it, or a stop)

db.description: `disconnected` answers 503 with this same body; `Not connected`: no database configured

503.description: this copy is shutting down (SIGTERM: a swap deploy retiring it, or a stop)

POST /v1/embeddings.$comment: OpenAI Embeddings: request checked against the box's GET /openapi.json (its documented model types `input` as a list of strings; the proxy passes a string through as OpenAI allows); 200 litellm.types.utils.EmbeddingResponse; the 404 from litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py at the v1.95.0 tag _handle_llm_api_exception + litellm/proxy/_types.py at the v1.95.0 tag ProxyException, its message as LiteLLM 1.95.0's Router raises it (reproduced locally against a stand-in for the vLLM 404); LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).
POST /v1/embeddings.description: No embedding model is configured in this deployment, so this answers an error today: every `model_list` backend is a chat (or TTS) server. The collection's `qwen3.6` reaches its vLLM server, which registers no `/v1/embeddings` for a chat model (FastAPI's 404 `{"detail": "Not Found"}`); LiteLLM (no retry for a 404) tries its `fallbacks` entry `claude-sonnet-5` (which it cannot embed with: `Unmapped LLM provider for this endpoint`) and answers the first error, a 404. With qwen3.6 down it is a 500 (connection error) instead. The 200 is what a model with an embedding backend would answer.

200.description: only from a model whose backend embeds (none configured)

embedding.description: Floats, or a base64 string with `encoding_format: base64`

404.description: today, for the collection's `qwen3.6`: its vLLM server has no embeddings route

message.description: `litellm.NotFoundError: NotFoundError: OpenAIException - Error code: 404 - {'detail': 'Not Found'}. Received Model Group=qwen3.6`, then the fallbacks tried and each one's error

code.description: The HTTP status, as a string

POST /v1/audio/speech.$comment: OpenAI Speech: request checked against the box's GET /openapi.json (which declares no body for it); response litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py at the v1.95.0 tag audio_speech; LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).

voice.description: An OpenAI alias or a Kokoro voice name

response_format.description: Ignored by Kokoro, which only makes WAV

200.description: the backend's audio bytes, labelled `audio/mpeg` by LiteLLM whatever they are (only a Gemini TTS model gets `audio/wav`): from kokoro they are WAV (`RIFF…WAVE`)

GET /user/info.$comment: UserInfoResponse from the box's GET /openapi.json; LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).

GET /model/info.$comment: litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py at the v1.95.0 tag model_info_v1 (the box's GET /openapi.json declares no body); LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).

GET /mcp/kokoro_tts.$comment: litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py at the v1.95.0 tag handle_streamable_http_mcp, which hands a GET to the MCP Python SDK's streamable-HTTP transport (mcp>=1.28.1; 1.29.0 read here: mcp/server/streamable_http.py _handle_get_request); LiteLLM v1.95.0 (ai/litellm/Dockerfile.litellm: FROM docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0; the box's container reports info.version 1.95.0).
GET /mcp/kokoro_tts.description: The URL to register (`claude mcp add --transport http … {{litellm}}/mcp/<server>`), not an API: MCP clients POST JSON-RPC here. A plain GET is the MCP stream a client opens for server-sent messages, so it needs `Accept: text/event-stream`; Postman's default `*/*` gets the 406. Every `/mcp/<server>` item answers alike, after LiteLLM's own checks: a bad key or one not allowed the server is its 401 / 403, and `gmail` (OAuth delegated to Google) answers a request with no bearer 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.

200.description: with `Accept: text/event-stream`: an open stream for server-to-client JSON-RPC messages, which on LiteLLM's stateless path (no `mcp-session-id`) carries nothing and never ends

message.const: Not Acceptable: Client must accept text/event-stream
